india_notes: Always show ₹ prices with a date stamp and the shop/site (Amazon, Flipkart, mdcomputers, PrimeABGB, Vedant, local shop). GPU prices in India rose ~30% on average Jul→Aug 2026 (RTX 5060 ~₹32.8K → ~₹46K, RTX 5050 ~₹28.8K → ~₹44K per TimesOfGames, 1 Sep 2026, single source). Re-check on shoot day.
RAM crisis in rupees: 32GB DDR5 kits listed ₹37–44K on Amazon India in Jun–Jul 2026 (Crucial ₹37,475; Patriot Viper ₹43,999). Say 'listing on <date>', not 'price'.

Sale calendar: Amazon Great Indian Festival from 8 Oct; Flipkart Big Bang Diwali Sale reported from ~28 Oct (dates differ by source, verify in-app); Diwali is 8 Nov 2026. 'Don't buy' and 'is this deal real?' reels peak in the 10 days before Diwali.
Core budget bands for Indian PC gamers: ₹50–60K entry, ₹75K–1L mainstream, ₹1.5L enthusiast. Laptops outsell desktops; 'gaming laptop' tips have a wider audience than desktop-only tips.
Hinglish rules: speak Hinglish, keep on-screen text mostly English with Hinglish punchlines in Latin script ('bhai', 'scene', 'paisa vasool'). Commands/paths always in exact English.

Local context jokes: power cuts and UPS, 38°C summer room temps and dust, '₹500 repair wale bhaiya', office laptop vs home rig, Pune traffic, chai-break analogies. Name Pune shops only if Srijan actually uses them.
Competitive games with Indian audiences: Valorant, CS2, BGMI (mobile), GTA V RP, LoL smaller. Use CS2/Valorant for latency tips (both support NVIDIA Reflex).
GST on PC components is 18% and import duties apply, which is why India lands above US MSRP: a fair 'why is it costlier here' explainer line.
Sponsored or affiliate posts must carry a clear disclosure label (ASCI influencer guidelines: 'Ad'/'Paid partnership' up front). The Brain has no ASCI notes yet (gap in trends.json).
Indian audiences save and share money-saving and 'don't get scammed' reels most; frame tips as rupees saved or repair visits avoided.
research.lane: The funny PC gamer next door from Pune who tests the hype on his own rig. Three formats he can own: (1) 'Ek Setting' one-tip fixes that open on a symptom and prove the result on screen; (2) 'Tech news, translated to FPS and ₹': what a GPU/CPU/Windows change means for an Indian gamer's frames and wallet, rumours labelled; (3) roast tier lists and skits (tips, GPUs, Windows features, shopkeeper POVs). Not a studio PC-build channel like Rahul Hinduja (builds/buying by budget) or a lab like Hardware Unboxed: Srijan's edge is settings + humour + his own rig + Hinglish, and it overlaps with his gaming lane (CS2/LoL clips as proof).

tips.title: Your 144Hz monitor might be running at 60Hz
tips.command: Settings > System > Display > Advanced display > Choose a refresh rate > pick the highest (e.g. 144/165/240Hz). In-game: set the same refresh and Fullscreen/Borderless.
tips.what: Windows (and a new cable/driver install) often defaults a high-refresh monitor to 60Hz.
tips.benefit: If it was wrong: motion goes from 60 to 144+ updates per second. Huge smoothness gain and lower display latency, zero cost. If it was already right: nothing changes.
tips.myth_check: Real. Also check the cable: HDMI 1.4 or a cheap cable can cap refresh; use DisplayPort or the cable that came with the monitor.
tips.film: Film the monitor with the iPhone: UFO-style moving test (testufo.com) at 60Hz vs 144Hz, phone in slo-mo 240fps to show the difference, then screen-record the Settings change. Screen-record the exact clicks at 1080p+ (Snipping Tool Win+Shift+R records any screen region incl. Settings; OBS for 60fps). Face cam: iPhone 15 on the tripod beside the monitor, 1x, 4K30, AE/AF lock. Edit as a screen card with a circular face cam; zoom 150–200% onto the toggle as you click; red→green text for before/after.

tips.title: Plug the monitor into the graphics card, not the motherboard
tips.command: Look at the back of the PC: the display cable must go into the ports on the horizontal GPU bracket (lower), not the vertical motherboard I/O ports (upper). Check: Task Manager > Performance > GPU 0/GPU 1 and see which GPU the game uses.
tips.what: Motherboard video outputs use the CPU's integrated graphics (or nothing at all).
tips.benefit: If it was wrong: often 2–10× more FPS instantly because the game moves from iGPU to the real GPU.
tips.myth_check: Real and very common with first builds.
tips.film: iPhone on tripod behind the PC with a torch; push-in on the two port areas; animated arrow overlay; then a before/after FPS counter (in-game or NVIDIA/AMD overlay).

tips.title: Turn on XMP/EXPO: your RAM is probably running slow
tips.command: Check: Ctrl+Shift+Esc > Performance > Memory > 'Speed' (e.g. 4800 MT/s vs the 6000 on the box). Fix: reboot into BIOS (shutdown /r /fw /t 0) > enable XMP (Intel) or EXPO (AMD) profile > Save & Exit.
tips.what: RAM runs at a safe default (JEDEC) speed until you enable the rated profile.
tips.benefit: Typically a few % to ~10% in CPU-bound games, better 1% lows; more on Ryzen. Varies by game and CPU.
tips.myth_check: Real, but update the BIOS first. If the PC fails to boot, it will usually retry with defaults; otherwise clear CMOS (motherboard manual). Not an overclock you need to tune.
tips.film: Screen-record Task Manager memory speed before/after; film the BIOS screen with the iPhone (BIOS can't be screen-recorded) with exposure locked down to avoid blown-out monitor.

tips.title: Game Mode: what it really does
tips.command: Settings > Gaming > Game Mode > On (default on).
tips.what: Prioritises the game's CPU/GPU resources and stops Windows Update from installing drivers or showing restart prompts while you play.
tips.benefit: Small; mainly fewer hitches when background tasks run. Not a magic FPS boost.
tips.myth_check: Old myth said it hurt FPS; that was early Windows 10. On Windows 11 keep it on.

tips.title: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (HAGS)
tips.command: Settings > System > Display > Graphics > Advanced/Change default graphics settings > Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling > On > restart (location varies by build).
tips.what: Lets the GPU manage its own memory scheduling instead of the CPU.
tips.benefit: Usually 0–a few % or none; required for NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation. Turn on if you use frame gen; otherwise test both.
tips.myth_check: Partly myth as an FPS booster; real as a frame-gen requirement.

tips.title: Optimizations for windowed games
tips.command: Settings > System > Display > Graphics > Change default graphics settings > Optimizations for windowed games > On.
tips.what: Switches older DirectX 10/11 games in borderless/windowed mode to the modern 'flip' presentation model.
tips.benefit: Lower latency in borderless mode and unlocks Auto HDR/VRR there. Not more FPS.
tips.myth_check: Real (Microsoft support doc). Auto HDR forces it on.

tips.title: Gaming laptop: make sure the game uses the real GPU
tips.command: Settings > System > Display > Graphics > select the game (Add desktop app if missing) > GPU preference: High performance. Plus in the vendor app (Armoury Crate/Legion Space/MSI Center/Omen) set GPU mode to Discrete/dGPU (MUX) or Ultimate, and play plugged in.
tips.what: Hybrid laptops can run games on the integrated GPU; MUX/discrete mode removes the iGPU pass-through.
tips.benefit: If the game was on the iGPU: massive gain. MUX/discrete: often ~5–15% more FPS and lower latency (varies by laptop).
tips.myth_check: Real. Switching MUX needs a restart; battery life drops in discrete mode.
tips.film: Screen-record Settings + vendor app; film the laptop with the charger plugging in as a punchline.

tips.title: Win+Ctrl+Shift+B restarts your graphics driver
tips.command: Press Windows + Ctrl + Shift + B together. Screen blinks black and beeps.
tips.what: Resets the graphics driver without rebooting.
tips.benefit: Fixes a frozen/black screen or a second monitor that won't wake, in 2 seconds. No FPS change.
tips.myth_check: Real. Doesn't fix a crashed game; it fixes the display path.
tips.film: Film keyboard close-up from above (hands POV) + the monitor blinking; it's visual and quick.

tips.title: Check Resizable BAR (Smart Access Memory)
tips.command: NVIDIA: NVIDIA Control Panel > System Information > Resizable BAR: Yes/No. AMD: Adrenalin > Performance > Tuning > Smart Access Memory. Any GPU: GPU-Z 'Resizable BAR'. To enable: BIOS > Above 4G Decoding On + Re-Size BAR On (CSM off, UEFI boot).
tips.what: Lets the CPU access the full GPU memory at once.
tips.benefit: 0–10% depending on the game (NVIDIA whitelists games); essential for Intel Arc cards (big losses without it).
tips.myth_check: Real but small on most NVIDIA setups. Turning off CSM can break boot on old Legacy/MBR installs: check msinfo32 'BIOS Mode: UEFI' first.
tips.film: Screen-record GPU-Z/driver panel; iPhone film the BIOS toggles.

tips.title: Restart straight into BIOS, no F2 spam
tips.command: Open Terminal (Admin) > shutdown /r /fw /t 0
tips.what: Tells the UEFI firmware to open its setup on the next boot and restarts immediately.
tips.benefit: Saves the 'which key, how fast' struggle; useful for XMP/ReBAR/fan curves.
tips.myth_check: Real. Needs UEFI mode (msinfo32 > BIOS Mode). Save your work first: it restarts instantly.
tips.film: Screen-record typing the command, then iPhone films the monitor landing in BIOS. Loopable.

tips.title: Bottleneck check that actually works
tips.command: In game: Win+G > Performance widget (or NVIDIA overlay Alt+R / AMD overlay Ctrl+Shift+O). GPU usage ~95–99% = GPU-bound (normal, good). GPU well below ~90% with one CPU thread pegged or low FPS = CPU/engine limit.
tips.what: Reads the live usage instead of guessing.
tips.benefit: Tells you whether lowering graphics settings or a better CPU will help.
tips.myth_check: Myth-bust: online 'bottleneck calculators' guess from part names and ignore the game, resolution and settings.
tips.film: Screen-record gameplay with the overlay in two scenarios (1080p low vs 1440p high) and point at GPU %.

tips.title: Smoothest combo: VRR on + cap FPS a few below refresh + Reflex
tips.command: Monitor OSD: FreeSync/Adaptive-Sync on. NVIDIA App > Graphics > Global: G-SYNC on, Max Frame Rate = refresh − 3 (141 on 144Hz); in game turn on NVIDIA Reflex if offered (CS2, Valorant). AMD: FreeSync on in Adrenalin, cap with Radeon Chill (min = max) or the in-game limiter, Anti-Lag on.
tips.what: Keeps FPS inside the VRR range so there's no tearing and no V-Sync queue.
tips.benefit: Smoother frame pacing and lower input lag than V-Sync alone. Doesn't raise FPS.
tips.myth_check: Real and widely tested (Blur Busters-style guidance). DLSS 4.5 Dynamic MFG currently doesn't work with frame limiters/V-Sync: turn the cap off there.
tips.film: Screen-record the settings; then side-by-side slow-mo phone footage of tearing vs smooth.

tips.title: DLSS/FSR/XeSS modes, decoded
tips.command: In game graphics settings: Upscaler = DLSS / FSR / XeSS; Mode = Quality / Balanced / Performance / Ultra Performance.
tips.what: Renders fewer pixels and AI/algorithm-upscales. Quality ≈ 67% of output resolution per axis, Balanced ≈ 58%, Performance 50%, Ultra Performance 33%.
tips.benefit: Large FPS gains. At 1440p/4K, Quality/Balanced look close to native; at 1080p, Performance gets soft.
tips.myth_check: 'Upscaling is always blurry' is outdated for DLSS 4.x/FSR 4.x; still true for old FSR 1/2 at 1080p.
tips.film: Pixel-grid motion graphic (HyperFrames) + in-game A/B crops zoomed 300%.

tips.title: Frame generation: smooth isn't the same as fast
tips.command: In game: DLSS Frame Generation / Multi Frame Generation (RTX 40/50; 3x–6x on RTX 50), FSR Frame Generation (AMD; ML version on RX 9000), XeSS-FG.
tips.what: AI draws extra frames between real ones. The counter goes up; your inputs are still read at the base frame rate.
tips.benefit: Great for single-player at ≥ ~50–60 base FPS on high-refresh screens. Adds some latency; bad idea in CS2/Valorant.
tips.myth_check: Myth: '240 FPS with frame gen = as responsive as real 240'. It isn't.
tips.film: Flipbook analogy with a real paper flipbook on desk + latency graph card; gameplay with overlay showing FPS and latency.

tips.title: Upgrade old games to the newest DLSS model (NVIDIA App)
tips.command: NVIDIA App > Graphics > pick the game (or Global) > DLSS Override – Model Presets > Latest/Recommended; then enable DLSS in the game.
tips.what: Swaps the game's old DLSS model for a newer transformer preset.
tips.benefit: Sharper, more stable image in older DLSS titles. Newest presets cost more performance on RTX 20/30.
tips.myth_check: Real, official. Game must be on NVIDIA's override list.

tips.title: RX 6000/7000 owners: free FSR 4.1 upgrade
tips.command: Install AMD Software Adrenalin 26.10.1 or newer > open a supported game's profile in Adrenalin > turn on the FSR 4 upgrade/override toggle (name can vary by driver) > choose FSR in game.
tips.what: Uses AMD's ML upscaler on older Radeons (RDNA 2 via an adapted INT8 model).
tips.benefit: Better image quality than FSR 3.1 at the same mode; some performance overhead on older cards (AMD hasn't published RX 6000 numbers).
tips.myth_check: Real (20 Oct 2026). Not on Xbox yet. Frame-gen ML upgrade is still RX 9000 only.

tips.title: Kill the apps that start with Windows
tips.command: Ctrl+Shift+Esc > Startup apps > sort by Startup impact > Disable launchers/updaters you don't need at boot (Steam/Epic/Discord can start later). Never disable your antivirus, audio or touchpad drivers.
tips.what: Stops apps loading at boot.
tips.benefit: Faster boot and less background RAM/CPU. Small or no FPS change on a strong PC; noticeable on 8GB laptops.
tips.myth_check: Real for boot time; 'more FPS' only if those apps were hogging resources.

tips.title: Update every app with one command
tips.command: Terminal > winget upgrade (lists updates) > winget upgrade --all
tips.what: Windows' built-in package manager updates installed apps from their official sources.
tips.benefit: Saves time and patches security holes in old apps.
tips.myth_check: Real. Some installers pop up UAC prompts or close the app; save work first. Skip apps you want pinned with winget pin.

tips.title: Repair Windows before you pay the repair guy
tips.command: Terminal (Admin): DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth then sfc /scannow, then restart.
tips.what: DISM repairs the system image; SFC then repairs protected system files from it.
tips.benefit: Fixes random crashes, broken Settings/Start, odd errors caused by corrupted system files. Not an FPS booster.
tips.myth_check: Real. Takes 5–20 minutes; don't close the window.

tips.title: Storage Sense: free GBs automatically
tips.command: Settings > System > Storage > Storage Sense > On; also Storage > Cleanup recommendations.
tips.what: Cleans temp files and the Recycle Bin on a schedule.
tips.benefit: Frees space; keep ~10–15% of an SSD free for performance and updates.
tips.myth_check: Check the 'Downloads' option (it can delete old downloads). Freeing space does not raise FPS unless the drive was nearly full.

tips.title: powercfg /energy: find what's draining power
tips.command: Terminal (Admin) > cd $env:USERPROFILE > powercfg /energy > open energy-report.html
tips.what: Traces the system for 60 seconds and reports power-efficiency errors (USB devices not suspending, power plan issues, apps blocking sleep).
tips.benefit: Diagnose bad battery life or a PC that won't sleep. Not a performance tweak.
tips.myth_check: Real diagnostic; read the red 'Errors' section only.

tips.title: Your laptop battery's real health in one command
tips.command: Terminal > powercfg /batteryreport > open battery-report.html > compare DESIGN CAPACITY vs FULL CHARGE CAPACITY.
tips.what: Windows logs battery capacity and cycle count.
tips.benefit: Know if the battery is worn before buying a used laptop or claiming warranty.
tips.myth_check: Real. Desktops have no battery: laptop-only tip.
tips.film: Screen-record the report; highlight the two numbers; ₹ angle: check before buying a second-hand laptop on OLX.

tips.title: Clip your clutch after it happens: Win+Alt+G
tips.command: Settings > Gaming > Captures > 'Record what happened' On (set 30s). In game press Win+Alt+G. NVIDIA: Instant Replay on (Alt+Shift+F10), save with Alt+F10. AMD: Ctrl+Shift+S with Instant Replay on.
tips.what: Keeps a rolling buffer and saves the last 30 seconds.
tips.benefit: Never miss a clip. Background recording costs a little performance (small on modern GPUs' hardware encoders).
tips.myth_check: Real. On a weak laptop, turn background recording off when you don't need it.
tips.film: Gaming clip (CS2/LoL) of a real play, then the shortcut on screen; ties into his gaming lane.

tips.title: Stop Windows uploading updates to strangers while you play
tips.command: Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Delivery Optimization > 'Allow downloads from other devices' Off (or Advanced options > limit upload bandwidth).
tips.what: Windows can share update files with other PCs over the internet using your upload.
tips.benefit: Less background upload on slow Indian broadband/hotspots. Updates still install normally.
tips.myth_check: Real. This does NOT turn off Windows Update (never do that).

tips.title: Win+V: clipboard history (and pin snippets)
tips.command: Press Win+V > Turn on. Pin your email/address/UPI ID.
tips.what: Keeps the last 25 copied items and pinned ones.
tips.benefit: Office + gaming efficiency: paste anything you copied earlier.
tips.myth_check: Real. Don't pin passwords/OTPs; history can sync if cloud sync is on.

tips.title: MYTH: ipconfig /flushdns lowers your ping
tips.command: DON'T expect: ipconfig /flushdns
tips.what: Clears cached DNS lookups.
tips.benefit: Fixes a site that won't resolve. Does nothing for in-game ping (that's route/server distance).
tips.myth_check: Myth for ping. Use a closer server region and wired Ethernet instead.
tips.film: Run it live, then show the ping counter unchanged; comedic 'nothing happened' beat.

tips.title: MYTH: the hidden 'Ultimate Performance' power plan boosts FPS
tips.command: DON'T expect: powercfg -duplicatescheme e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61
tips.what: Unhides a workstation power plan.
tips.benefit: On desktops: within margin of error in games, higher idle power. On laptops plugged in, Windows 'Best performance' mode does the job.
tips.myth_check: Mostly placebo for gaming. Use Settings > System > Power > Power mode > Best performance on laptops.
tips.film: Benchmark run before/after with identical results card.

tips.title: MYTH: disable all services / run a random 'FPS booster' script
tips.command: DON'T: services.msc mass-disable, unknown .bat/registry 'optimizer' packs
tips.what: Turns off Windows components.
tips.benefit: Little to no FPS on modern PCs; can break Windows Update, audio, Bluetooth, printing, Microsoft Store, anti-cheat.
tips.myth_check: Myth + risk. Random scripts from comments can contain malware. If you must, use a well-known open-source tool, read every option, and make a restore point.
tips.film: Tier list 'D tier' entry with a warning stamp; no live demo.

tips.title: MYTH: turn off Defender / Memory Integrity / updates for free FPS
tips.command: DON'T: disable Windows Security, Memory Integrity or Windows Update
tips.what: Removes security protections.
tips.benefit: Defender: near-zero FPS cost on modern PCs. Memory Integrity: can cost a few % (more on older CPUs) but protects the kernel from malicious drivers.
tips.myth_check: We never recommend this. Check status in Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation details; keep it on. If a game breaks, update its anti-cheat/drivers first.
tips.film: Show the status screen only; say 'leave it on'.

tips.title: MYTH: clear your shader cache for more FPS
tips.command: DON'T routinely: delete NVIDIA/AMD/DirectX shader cache
tips.what: Deletes compiled shaders.
tips.benefit: Games must recompile them: more stutter for the next sessions. Only clear to fix a corrupted cache after a driver issue. NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D settings > Shader Cache Size: Driver Default or 10GB+.
tips.myth_check: Myth for FPS.
tips.film: Frame-time graph spike after clearing (CapFrameX or in-game graph).

tips.title: MYTH: NVIDIA 'Prefer maximum performance' = more FPS
tips.command: NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D settings > Power management mode
tips.what: Stops the GPU dropping clocks at light loads.
tips.benefit: In demanding games the GPU already boosts; the main effect is higher idle/desktop power. Can help a few esports titles with clock-drop stutter.
tips.myth_check: Mostly myth; per-game only if you see clock drops.
tips.film: Overlay clocks in a heavy game: same either way.

tips.title: MYTH: deleting Temp/Prefetch makes games faster
tips.command: DON'T expect: deleting %temp% / C:\Windows\Prefetch for FPS
tips.what: Removes temp files and app-launch hints.
tips.benefit: Frees a little space; Prefetch actually speeds app launches and Windows rebuilds it.
tips.myth_check: Myth. Use Storage Sense instead.

Win10 without ESU won't receive new certs. Don't disable Secure Boot. Valorant's Vanguard requires Secure Boot/TPM on Windows 11.

steps.do: Set up the face cam at the desk
steps.detail: Tripod at seated eye height (~110–120 cm), phone vertical, 1x lens, 4K 30fps, HDR Video off. Sit ~60–80 cm away, monitor glow as key light from the front-side plus a warm lamp behind for depth (RGB on low, one colour). Long-press to lock AE/AF on your face and drag exposure −0.3 so the screen doesn't blow out. Leave headroom/space above your head for graphics.

Windows Update page and Windows Security > Device security (Secure Boot indicator). Use Snipping Tool (Win+Shift+R → select full screen → Start) or OBS at 1080p/1440p 60fps. Set Windows display scaling so text is readable on a phone (125–150%), dark mode on, close personal tabs/notifications (Focus on). Move the mouse slowly; pause 1 s on every click so the zoom has time to land.

steps.do: Build the screen-card + circular face-cam layout in CapCut desktop
steps.detail: Canvas 9:16 1080×1920. Screen recording scaled into a rounded dark card in the middle third; face cam masked to a circle (≈380 px) bottom-left above the caption safe zone, thin yellow ring. Keyframe 150–200% zooms onto each toggle exactly as it's clicked (ease-out, ~8 frames). Hard-cut between full-face (hook/verdict) and card layout so something changes every 1.5–2.5 s. Cut every breath/pause.

Frame-1 hook text (≤8 words, yellow condensed caps, top-centre inside safe zone): "SECURE BOOT: EXPIRED?". Word-by-word white captions with the key word highlighted (CapCut Auto captions → fix Hinglish spellings by hand). Exact command/path shown as a monospace label for ≥2 s so viewers can screenshot it. Keep text out of the top ~250 px, bottom ~350 px and the right-hand button rail.

Voice-led, no trending track needed: quiet lo-fi/synth bed at about −22 dB under the voice; UI click on every toggle, whoosh on layout swaps, soft 'ding' on the result, thud on the punchline. Denoise the voice lightly (CapCut 'Reduce noise'), normalise the export to around −14 LUFS. Use real recorded SFX (library/ or Mixkit), not synthesized beeps.

1080×1920, 30fps (60fps if the screen recording/gameplay is 60), high bitrate, no watermark. Final assembly in Edits if you want in-app audio or text styles, then post from Edits/Instagram. Cross-post a native re-edit to YouTube Shorts (title = searchable question).

Post weekday 7–9 PM IST. Cover = the result frame with the big number/setting name + your face (face-check: mouth closed, eyes open). Keyword-rich caption (first line = the problem as people search it). Share to Stories with a poll, reply to every comment in the first 60 minutes, pin a comment with the exact command/path. Once past 1,000 followers, test a second hook as a Trial Reel. YouTube Shorts title: 'Secure Boot certificate expired? What to do (Windows 11/10)'.

ideas.caption:

✅ Install Windows Updates (and your PC maker's BIOS update if offered)
✅ Check Windows Security > Device security
❌ Don't disable Secure Boot (anti-cheat games need it)
⚠️ Windows 10 without ESU won't get the new certificates.
